hypothesis: Compared with the valid four-accumulator parent, eight independent per-thread streams halve the full-group loop trips and may improve instruction-level parallelism while preserving the 1024-CTA, 256-thread lane ownership, input coverage, partial count, and finalizer. Extra live accumulators may instead increase register pressure; controller correctness and full-call measurements will decide.
notes: This changes only the per-thread streaming grouping. The parent and recent tail-handling candidate are valid, but their close measurements do not establish a meaningful speedup. No correctness or performance result is claimed for this candidate; controller validation should include every required size, seed, FP64 error bound, and full-call timing.
transformations: Keep 1024 CTAs, 256 threads per CTA, per-lane starting indices, global stride, 1024 partials, and the existing CUB finalizer unchanged.
Replace four independent per-thread accumulators with eight, processing complete groups without per-element bounds checks and checking the remaining tail loads individually.
Retain the two-kernel fused absolute-sum topology and write each partial and output on every call.
